brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. The namesake is the biggest region in the world and it is ONE room. Priced on HEAD in buildGrid's x<64 branch: the walled garden is x 3..61 by y 3..61 — 3,364 cells, 28% of the world — and its floor is a linden at r<1.15, a round lawn out to gR(th) (17.2 +- ~4), one ring bed between bedIn/bedOut, and a perimeter BED band 1.6-3.0 cells deep against the wall. Everything else, on the order of 1,800 cells, is undifferentiated PATH: the largest single continuous surface in the town. Because the lawn is a CIRCLE inside a SQUARE that paving is deepest in the four CORNERS — roughly 9-10 cells of bare flag on each diagonal between the lawn's edge and the wall bed. c308 measured what that costs: seed 42, autumn day 65, 12.98 h, cloud 0.03, 73 people in town and about SIX in the walled garden. #186 answered that with a roof and #198 with rain; both were events, and the loop's own note says FABRIC BEATS EVENTS for a thirty-second visitor. So: give the garden a SECOND ROOM. Take ONE corner — the deadest ground in the world — enclose it with a clipped hedge that has an arched way through, and give the ground inside it a different job from the ground outside, the way a walled garden this size actually works (frames, a dipping tank, a nursery bed, standing pots). Count the PATH cells first and quote the number.
successLooksLike: From the wide shot the garden reads as TWO places rather than one — a line of clipped hedge with a way through it, and behind it ground that is visibly doing a different job. census tileKinds moves off 174 for the first time since #192, and any ground the new tile is cut OUT of is declared in __census's comments the way LEADS (#170), ARCADE (#186) and REED (#155) are, so developed/green stay honest.
avoid: Do NOT make the divider a WALL cell: buildVolumes puts a roof on every footprint, and #119 put the field hedge on the ground cache for exactly that reason (drawFieldEdge, FIELD_X/FIELD_H/FIELD_GAP — read it, it is the precedent and most of the drawing). A hedge that must divide ROUTING has to be in the grid; a hedge that only has to be SEEN does not. Pick one and say which. If it goes in the grid, remember the law: a non-walkable cell holds only where a route's ENDPOINTS are chosen — grep the READERS of every predicate you widen, not its callers, and check lawnGate, gardNearest, BENCH_SPOTS and the arch entrances. Do NOT re-texture the existing paving: #212 already gave the court's flags moss and paveWear and more of that is rung 2. One corner done properly beats four done thinly.
